reason: The stored texts are real and useful: one frozen checklist replaces stale cron and timer prompts, and the facts match local state. Kernel ids and code sha8 match kernel-metadata.json for all 5 files. No NEVER_SUBMIT.md exists. Families match (89r/75/83c safetail_ci, 89q/89p safetail). exp_token is right on all 5 -m texts, and no night token appears in any earlier submission in poll.log. The [R29] L_hi correction matches tools/runtime_ledger.py l.197-199 (header + 210 s x failed attempts), which fixes the inverted form in the 20:18Z (c) text. The checklist sha256[:8] is 075152c4. It is not ready as stored, though, because nb_try fails OPEN. kaggle 2.2.4 (kaggle_api_extended.py l.9117-9129) prints 'Warning: Looks like you're using an outdated `kaggle` version ...' to STDOUT whenever the server's API version is newer. nb_try captures 2>&1, and grep '^ref,' still passes. csv.DictReader then takes the warning as the header, x['description'] raises KeyError, and python exits 1, which nb_try reads as 'token absent' and so SUBMITS. In a mock test the list with the warning gave rc=1 and the clean list rc=0. At the idempotent 00:20/00:44/00:50/01:30Z re-runs this re-submits files already sent and uses up the 2 morning slots (5/day). The T54 snippet uses the same parser: on a crash T54 is empty, and `date -u -d ""` = 00:00Z (tested), so the waiter fires at once and exp89p goes before the 40-min non-CI spacing. The trigger is conditional (0 such lines in poll.log today) but real and cheap to close.
fix: Before the 23:33Z freeze, edit night_checklist.md and then take the sha8. (1) In nb_try, make the dedupe fail closed: python reads stdin, keeps only the text from the first line that starts with 'ref,', exits 0 if the token is found and 10 if it is absent, and exits 2 on any exception. In bash: rc=$?; [ $rc -eq 0 ] && ALREADY; [ $rc -ne 10 ] && { echo PARSE FAIL; continue; }. (2) Apply the same 'start at ref,' slice to the G2 and T54 parsers, and add `[ -n "$T54" ] || T54=<exp89q submit + 40 min, or 2026-09-29T00:46:00Z>` before the waiter. (3) Optionally, in nb_try, send stderr of the list call to /dev/null (keep 2>&1 only for the LIST FAIL message). Re-run bash -n and the mock tests: warning-first list -> ALREADY or PARSE FAIL, never SUBMIT; empty T54 -> fallback time. Then put the new sha8 in freeze item (10).
realistic_gain: Operational only, no LB gain. It keeps an overnight kaggle-version warning from double-submitting night files, which would cost the 1-2 morning probe slots (MORNING TABLE v1.1 M1/M2), and from sending exp89p early. It takes about 10 minutes and changes no submitted file.
